budget.note: --cap is forbidden on the skill track (match-runner.mjs:193); the ceiling is enforceable only between games. SWP-03 is the only mechanism that can honour it, which is why every provider node depends on it. THREE stages share this one ceiling, in order: PIL-01 (shakeout, not rankable), CAL-03 (calibration corpus), RUN-02 (the ranked sweep). The ceiling is the total across all three, not per stage. CHANGED 2026-07-26 (human): runs go through a local sublet subscription proxy, not metered openrouter.ai, and run-with-sublet.sh clears OPENROUTER_API_KEY so a run meant to be free cannot quietly fall back to billing. usage.cost is still populated but is now a MODELLED price -- what the call would have cost metered -- so the ceiling stops being a bill and becomes a runaway-usage brake. Keep it: the accounting is still the efficiency metric, and an imputed 60 dollars of tokens is still a signal that something has gone wrong. Do not read spend columns in a published table as money changing hands.

nodes.title: Mint the benchmark-lockstep era lock: extend eraFiles, add benchmark identity
rationale: era-lock.mjs:38-41 states that changing the pinned file list is itself
era-defining, so this decision is the coordinator's. None of the benchmark
surfaces are pinned today. Also asserts the six scattered copies of
benchmark-lockstep-v1 agree, so the spec version cannot silently split.
MINTED LAST BY CONSTRUCTION: every node that edits a surface this lock will
pin must land first, or the lock drifts the moment the next node commits.
That is why this depends on ERA-03, the INT track and CAL-01 rather than
gating them.
PIN LIST IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN (revised 2026-07-26). An earlier draft named a
hand-picked ~21 surfaces. Checking it against the tree showed it was wrong in
two ways that would have shipped a benchmark whose era identity ignores things
the models demonstrably read:
(a) OpenRA.Browser.csproj sets no explicit Compile items and does not disable
default compile items, so ALL 27 AgentMode/*.cs are compiled into the
served assembly. The draft pinned 8. Unpinned were AgentSpatialSummary.cs
and AgentFogMemory.cs, which shape what the model can SEE, plus the whole
doctrine layer, which changed 10 times in the last 30 commits.
(b) strategy-catalog.ts reads ra-arsenal.json (:177), strategies/catalog.json,
situation-manual.json (:190) and 4 strategy cards at RUNTIME. None are
pinned and none are doctrines, so the unit stats table the models reason
from is invisible to era identity. doctrineHashes covers only
knowledge/playbooks/*.md.
The rule, applied mechanically at mint time: pin every file that is compiled
into the served agent assembly, executed by the sidecar, read as model-facing
knowledge, or is the benchmark's own player or scheduler. That is AgentMode/**,
agent-sidecar/src/**, agent-sidecar/knowledge/** except playbooks/ (already
covered by doctrineHashes), wwwroot/index.html + wwwroot/*.js except the
standalone s3/s4audio demo pages that index.html never loads, and
tests/benchmark-scripted-anchor.mjs + tests/benchmark-series-lib.mjs. Roughly 50
surfaces. Also asserts the scattered copies of benchmark-lockstep-v1 agree, so
the spec version cannot silently split.
RETRY BUDGET IS 12, NOT THE DEFAULT 2, and the reason is the point of the node.
ERA-02 is DESIGNED to fail every time a pinned surface moves. On 2026-07-26 it
failed twice in an hour, both times correctly: INT-05 edited server.ts and
INT-06 edited benchmark-series-lib.mjs, and each time the committed lock stopped
reproducing from the tree and the gate said so by name. Two strikes escalated it
and the driver stopped asking. A budget that treats the era lock noticing a
changed measured surface as unreliability defeats the lock. The fix each time is
a one-command re-mint, so the failure is informative and self-healing.
FOR INF-07, which is deferred: an escalated node has no documented way back. The
only in-band route here was to raise this budget. That is honest but it is not a
protocol, and INF-07 should define one.
Deliberately NOT pinned: match-runner.mjs, because it is the code that VALIDATES
the lock -- pinning it makes every future era definition self-invalidating.
The previous exclusion of AgentAdjudication.cs is dropped: it was justified by a
claim about its callers that turned out to be wrong once already, and a rule that
pins the whole compiled surface does not need that judgment call to be right.

gate.expectStdout: OK the benchmark-lockstep era lock pins every measured surface

Add the flags to the incompatibility block and make scoreGame refuse any

nodes.title: Stamp and assert the effective decision interval
rationale: wwwroot/index.html:209's agent-interval value="250" seeds decisionIntervalTicks
on the lockstep track; match-runner overrides it only for --staff-seat, which
lockstep forbids. Editing that one HTML attribute halves or doubles how many
paired decisions fit the tick horizon, for every model, with no visibility
anywhere in the evidence.
CORRECTED 2026-07-26: an earlier draft of this rationale called index.html the
ONLY source. It is not. AgentModeHost.cs:503 computes the value it actually
uses via AgentCadence.EffectiveDecisionInterval, and neither AgentMatchStartResult
nor AgentMatchState exposed the result, so requested and effective could differ
silently. Stamping the DOM value would have satisfied this gate while proving
nothing. Stamp the value the host ACTUALLY USED -- reusing the already-computed
field, never recomputing at stamp time -- carry it into outcome.json, and have
the series lib REJECT any game whose host-reported value differs from the
manifest. Absence at benchmark start is a hard failure, never a default.

A 36-game sweep is 12-16 hours of paid wall clock. Port ladder-runner's ledger,
--resume, fresh-start guard and resolved|unfinished|infrastructure-censored
taxonomy. Hard prerequisite for spending money.
NOT hypothetical: 19 of 41 existing match-results directories have a log.jsonl
and no outcome.json — a 46% historical abort rate. Over 36 games that is a
near-certainty, not a risk.
Two specific holes this node must close. (1) executeSweep reads
match-results/<label>/outcome.json unconditionally after every game, so a dead
page takes the whole series down with it. (2) match-runner.mjs:1232 sets
infrastructureCensored from providerTerminal ALONE, so a crashed page, a lost
WebGL context (BrowserGL2Window.cs:47-52 throws rather than degrading, and a
tab suspend or GPU reset during a multi-hour sweep will hit it) or a watchdog
kill is not classified at all. A game that died for harness reasons must be
retryable and must never be scored or charged as a model result.

nodes.title: Make the sweep payload publishable: evidence retention, tracked in git
rationale: FOUND 2026-07-26, and it is a defect in the terminal state itself. .gitignore:68
ignores OpenRA.Browser/tests/match-results/ wholesale: `git ls-files` returns ZERO
tracked files under it, and match-results/LEADERBOARD.md -- the single artifact
RUN-03 exists to change -- is present on disk and absent from git. A benchmark
whose pitch is 'reproducible from checked-in artifacts' currently cannot check in
the artifact. Every outcome.json, metrics.json, scorecard and era stamp from both
paid stages would live only on one laptop.
Not solved by tracking everything: 36 games of screenshots is hundreds of
megabytes, and log.jsonl carries raw provider traffic, which is a retention AND a
key-exposure question rather than a size one. Settle a policy -- what is evidence
that backs a rating, what is bulk, and what must never be committed -- express it
as .gitignore exceptions, and gate it: given a completed series directory, every
file the leaderboard derives a number from must be tracked, and nothing matching
the never-commit set may be.
Deliberately blocks both paid nodes. Settling this after the money is spent means
hand-curating the evidence that is supposed to prove the ratings.

gate.expectStdout: OK the published evidence set is complete, tracked, and free of never-commit files

nodes.title: Shakeout pilot: prove the paid path with real money before the corpus
rationale: A human decision of 2026-07-26 that the graph did not represent, so the graph
would have driven CAL-02 straight into a paid corpus. One seed pair, one cheap
matchup, about 4 games, roughly $2-4 of the $60.
DELIBERATELY NOT RANKABLE: the clustered CI needs at least 3 pairs, so this
cannot and must not produce a rating. Its only job is to prove that resume,
budget reservation, era stamping, crash classification and scoring survive
contact with real money and a real provider -- every one of which has so far
only been exercised against scripted fixtures.
Kept separate from CAL-03 so a plumbing bug cannot contaminate the calibration
corpus and force it to be paid for twice. The gate must assert the pilot
produced era-stamped, re-scorable results AND that it claims no ranking, because
a pilot that quietly looked rankable is the failure mode worth guarding.
CORRECTED 2026-07-26 -- this node could not have run as first written. It was
specified as a small sweep, but benchmark-series-lib.mjs:65 requires a
calibration with status=frozen and CAL-05 does not freeze one until after
CAL-03. A pilot scheduled before the freeze can therefore never resolve a
sweep. That is not a bug in the guard; the guard is right.
So the pilot runs as direct match-runner invocations, not a sweep:
--benchmark-lockstep --era-lock with NO --benchmark-calibration, which
match-runner.mjs:147/363 already treats as optional. That produces era-stamped
outcome.json with raw component ledgers and no score, which is precisely what
'deliberately not rankable' should mean mechanically rather than by intention.
Scoring happens later from those raw outcomes once floors are frozen -- SWP-02's
--score-only path exists for exactly that.
The sweep-level mechanics it was meant to prove -- resume, budget reservation,
crash classification -- are already proven by SWP-01/02/03 against fixtures. What
only real money and a real provider can prove, and what this node is now for, is
the live path: proxy to sidecar to host to an era-stamped outcome, with INT-05's
per-decision proof that the model named in the evidence is the model that
answered. Series id must begin benchmark-lockstep-v1- or INF-08's retention
policy will not track the evidence it produces.
SECOND CORRECTION 2026-07-26, from the live demo match: moving this node to direct
match-runner invocations to dodge the frozen-calibration requirement also threw away
the crash protection SWP-01 built. classifySweepAttempt (benchmark-sweep-runner.mjs:506)
classifies harness deaths and retries them; a bare match-runner invocation has nothing.
Proved by the demo: the headed browser window closed at tick 21173 after 17 good minutes
and the run died on page.evaluate with no outcome.json written. 19 accepted decisions of
real work, unrecoverable. The pilot needs its own crash handling, or a way to reach the
sweep path without a frozen calibration. Do not run PIL-01 until that is settled.

gate.expectStdout: OK the shakeout pilot proved the paid path end to end and claims no ranking

nodes.title: Prove the model that answered is the model on the leaderboard
rationale: REQUIRED BY THE MOVE TO A SUBSCRIPTION PROXY (human decision 2026-07-26): all
runs now go through a local sublet proxy at OPENROUTER_BASE_URL rather than
openrouter.ai, and the pool is x-ai/grok-4.5 + z-ai/glm-5.2 + the scripted
anchor.
server.ts:527/774 SEND a model and never read one back. Nothing anywhere in the
harness compares the model that answered against the model that was asked for.
That was survivable against a single metered endpoint; it is not survivable now.
sublet CAN resolve an unknown slug down a ladder to a default model, which
would publish a rating for grok-4.5 that claude-haiku-4.5 actually earned. It
reports such a swap honestly as sublet.substituted_for -- but only to something
that looks, and nothing in this harness looks.
Two guards already exist and neither is sufficient. Probed 2026-07-26: the
running proxy REFUSES an unknown model with HTTP 400 rather than substituting,
and run-with-sublet.sh re-probes that at startup and will not launch a sidecar
against a substituting proxy. Both are start-time facts about a configuration.
Neither is evidence about a decision that was recorded three hours later, and
neither survives a backend that changes behaviour mid-series. The published
claim is per-match, so the proof has to be per-match too.
Verified by probe before writing this: both pool models answer through the
OpenRouter dialect, return their true id, need no repair path (strict
json_schema returns clean conformant JSON for both, so neither model is
disadvantaged by a different structured-output route), and route-pinned slugs
grok:x-ai/grok-4.5 / zai:z-ai/glm-5.2 resolve to the canonical id with no colon
leaking downstream. Pin the route so a dead backend fails loudly instead of
substituting.
Two things to record, both absent today: the served model per decision, and the
ENDPOINT PROVENANCE. The era lock pins 53 source surfaces but not the endpoint,
so 'grok-4.5 via subscription proxy' and 'grok-4.5 via metered OpenRouter' are
indistinguishable in the evidence while being different competitors.
A substituted seat is INFRASTRUCTURE-CENSORED, never a model failure and never a
silent success -- scoring a swap as a loss would libel the model that never
played.
Touches agent-sidecar/src/server.ts, which ERA-02 pins, so the era lock must be
re-minted after this lands. ERA-02 now watches every pinned surface directory,
so the driver marks it stale by itself rather than relying on anyone remembering.

gate.expectStdout: OK every recorded decision proves which model and which route answered

nodes.title: Forbid cross-match lessons on the skill track, and record that they were absent
rationale: match-runner.mjs:204/206/208 reject --executor, --arsenal and --guided under
--benchmark-lockstep with 'the skill track is raw'. --lessons is NOT in that
list, and benchmark-series-lib.mjs:26 AssistanceFields is
[arsenal, executor, guided, fallbackStrike, play, staffSeat] -- lessons is
absent there too. So a lockstep match run with --lessons on injects prior-match
learnings into the seat prompt, and produces an outcome.json that is
indistinguishable from a clean one. scoreGame would accept it.
PROJECT-AUDIT-2026-07-16.md item 10 names the harm: lessons files are global per
model, so they leak across opponents and make results order-dependent -- in a
track whose entire claim is that it measures raw model skill under identical
conditions.
Swept games are safe today only BY OMISSION: benchmark-series-lib.mjs never
passes --lessons when it builds match argv. That is not a mechanism, it is a
coincidence of the current call site, and INT-02 exists precisely because raw
purity should not depend on one.
It became live rather than theoretical when PIL-01 was corrected to run DIRECT
match-runner invocations instead of a sweep: the pilot bypasses the very argv
construction that was accidentally protecting us.
Two halves, and the second matters as much as the first: REFUSE --lessons under
--benchmark-lockstep, and add lessons to the recorded assistance block so an
outcome PROVES it ran without them. A refusal alone leaves older or
hand-edited outcomes unfalsifiable.

gate.expectStdout: OK cross-match lessons cannot enter the skill track undetected

nodes.title: Structure loss must count possession, not death
rationale: FOUND by the adversarial validity audit 2026-07-26 and independently confirmed
at high confidence. This is the one defect found so far that can invert a
published winner, and it falsifies the benchmark's own anti-gaming claim at
README-BENCHMARK.md:129.
AgentAdjudicationLedger.RecordDestroyed has exactly ONE call site,
AgentModeHost.NotifyKilled (:341), reached only via AgentDamageObserver's
INotifyKilled. Selling ends at Sell.cs:56 self.Dispose() -- no Kill(), so
INotifyKilled never fires. Capture ends at CaptureActor.cs:122 ChangeOwnerSync --
also no kill. OpenRA.Browser implements INotifySold, INotifyActorDisposing and
INotifyOwnerChanged exactly zero times, so no compensating sensor exists.
A seat's structuresByValue component IS opponent.StructureLossValue
(AgentAdjudicationLedger.cs:196), so a player who SELLS each threatened building
instead of losing it keeps their own loss at zero and collapses the attacker's
20% component.
It pays the seller three times: the refund routes to GiveCash with isRefund
FALSE so it increments PlayerResources.Earned and is booked as incomePerMinute
inside the 20% ECONOMY component; ^Building carries SpawnActorsOnSell
(mods/ra/rules/defaults.yaml:752) at ValuePercent 40, returning ~40% of the value
as mobile AttackBase infantry that adds to the 25% LIVE POWER and can add REGION
OCCUPANCY; and the structure loss itself vanishes.
Reachable in exactly the ranked configuration: sell is in the model-facing action
catalog (host:1437), the contract manifest (:1752), applied with NO benchmark
gate (:6887), and the host ships a SellRefundEstimate in the raw observation
(AgentSituationEngine.cs:478, unguarded).
Measured against the current candidate floors: a 0.270 swing in S, against a
0.10 draw band. A game the attacker won publishes as a loss.
THE PRINCIPLE, not a patch to one path: a structure that leaves its owner's
possession is an irreversible loss to that owner, whatever removed it. Death is
one mechanism, not the definition. Capture is simultaneously a loss for the
original owner and a gain for the capturer.
CONSTRAINT: do not patch upstream engine files. Observers in AgentMode/
implementing OpenRA's notification interfaces are the shape; AgentDamageObserver
is the precedent. If refund-as-income cannot be fixed without an engine patch,
that must be reported rather than reached for.

gate.expectStdout: OK structure loss counts possession and cannot be zeroed by selling

nodes.title: The leaderboard must partition by track, not by era alone
rationale: FOUND by the validity audit 2026-07-26, confirmed. leaderboard.mjs:157
partitions era tables by eraLock.lockHash ALONE. BENCHMARK.md states the raw and
assisted tracks are never pooled, but nothing in the partition key encodes the
track, so both land in one W-L / Wilson / Elo table.
That is the single confound the whole two-track design exists to prevent: an
assisted result credits the model for what the harness did, and pooling it with
raw results means a better controller is published as a better model.
Publication-time defect, so it blocks RUN-03 rather than the pilot.

gate.expectStdout: OK no published table pools two tracks or two eras

nodes.title: A wall-clock safety stop must be censored, not scored
rationale: FOUND by the validity audit 2026-07-26, confirmed. match-runner.mjs:1363 ends a
match on the wall-clock safety stop and the result is scored as an ordinary
horizon-capped game rather than censored.
The cut tick therefore depends on how fast the MACHINE was, not on how the game
went, and that machine-dependent cut feeds the composite. Two runs of the same
seeded matchup on different hardware can produce different scores, which breaks
the reproducibility claim directly.
Blocks PIL-01: this is match-time classification, so a pilot run under it
produces evidence that cannot be rescued by re-scoring later.

gate.expectStdout: OK a wall-clock safety stop is censored and never scored

nodes.title: The barrier must not wake a seat on its opponent's private alert
rationale: FOUND by the validity audit 2026-07-26, confirmed. Under lockstep the union
trigger at AgentModeHost.cs:2664 wakes BOTH seats when either one's trigger
fires. A seat whose own trigger is idle is therefore woken by its opponent's
PRIVATE alert -- and is told so, as decisionTrigger:'paired' in its observation.
That is a fog leak through the barrier itself: the timing of an opponent's alert
is information about the opponent's situation that the seat has not earned. Worse
than a raw timing side channel, because it is labelled.
The barrier exists to remove latency from the score, not to synchronise
knowledge. Equal decision OPPORTUNITIES is the requirement; equal decision
CAUSES is not.
Blocks PIL-01: a match played under the leak is contaminated at generation time
and no amount of re-scoring repairs it.

gate.expectStdout: OK a paired wake leaks nothing about why the other seat woke

nodes.title: Pin the rules that denominate every score component
rationale: FOUND by the validity audit 2026-07-26, confirmed, and it is a hole in MY OWN
53-surface derivation. Not to be confused with the ERA-04 proposal declined
earlier (relaxing era-lock's engineCommit check); that was a different node and
is still declined.
era-surfaces.mjs derives the pin list from what is agent-FACING: compiled into
the served assembly, executed by the sidecar, read as model knowledge. It does
not include the engine or the mod rules. But mods/ra/rules defines Valued.Cost,
which is the unit EVERY score component is denominated in -- structure value,
unit value, replacement cost, tech value.
So editing a cost in mods/ra/rules produces ZERO drift and pools the new games
with the old corpus under an identical lockHash, while every published number
silently changes meaning. era1 died of an incomplete pin list and this is the
same failure one level down: I fixed which agent files are pinned and missed
that the scoreboard's units are defined elsewhere.
Decide deliberately how far this reaches -- the full mods/ tree is large and
most of it does not touch scoring -- but a rule that pins nothing of the
ruleset is indefensible for a benchmark whose scores are denominated in it.

gate.expectStdout: OK the era pins the rules its scores are denominated in
